rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law (interest, notice, and return of security deposits)
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay tenants the interest earned on security deposits, give written notice of where the deposit is held, and return the deposit with interest less itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends (5 business days if the tenant is displaced by fire, flood, condemnation or evacuation). A landlord who wrongfully withholds a deposit may owe double the amount withheld plus costs and attorney's fees.
rules.key_value: Return within 30 days of termination of tenancy; double damages for wrongful withholding
rules.penalty: Double the amount wrongfully withheld plus court costs and attorney's fees; civil penalty of $500 to $2,000 per offense for willfully withholding the deposit of a tenant receiving government assistance; disorderly-person charge with a fine of at least $200 or up to 30 days imprisonment for unlawful use of deposit monies.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential landlords holding tenant security deposits, including after a sale or transfer of the property.

rules.quoted_span: Within 30 days after the termination of a tenancy, a landlord must return the security deposit, plus interest earned less deductions, to the tenant ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.1).

rules.title: Rent Control/Rent Increases in New Jersey (Anti-Eviction Act notice and unconscionability standard; Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law)
rules.requirement: The State sets no rent control. Municipalities may adopt rent control ordinances, and a landlord may raise rent only by terminating the lease and giving proper written notice. The increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with local ordinances. Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years, and rents may not be raised to cover costs of a condominium or cooperative conversion.
rules.key_value: No state cap; newly constructed multiple dwellings exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion

coverage.summary: State notice and unconscionability rules apply to residential rent increases, with any rent caps set by municipal ordinance.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Newly constructed multiple dwellings are exempt from local rent control for 30 years after completion of construction, and government-subsidized rents may also be exempt.

precedence.text: Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.

rules.quoted_span: The State of New Jersey has no laws that establish, govern or control rents. Municipalities may pass an ordinance establishing rent control or rent leveling.
